greek: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἰσῆλθεν Μωυσῆς καὶ Ααρων πρὸς Φαραω καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τάδε λέγει κύριος ὁ θεὸς Ισραηλ Ἐξαπόστειλον τὸν λαόν μου, ἵνα μοι ἑορτάσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.
hint: Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh with the lord's demand: release the people to hold a festival in the desert.

notes.text: The singular, with two subjects, agreeing with the first; the Hebrew bāʾû is plural.
ἑορτάζω, to keep festival, for the Hebrew wĕyāḥōggû, that they may hold a feast.

reading: and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] and [[name:Ααρων]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Φαραω]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to him [[these|these, the immediate present, here and on the spot, thus, hither and to this spot, therefore and on this account|ὅδε]] [[says|says, speaks, declares, calls by name, tells|λέγω]] [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[send quite away|send quite away, dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] of me, [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] to me [[may keep festival|may keep festival and holiday, may celebrate as and by a festival|ἑορτάζω]] [[in the desert part|within, inside of, and by means of the desert part, the desolate and lone and lonely and lonesome and solitary, the desolate and helpless, the reft of and void, the destitute of, the wanting and without, the undefended|ἐν; ἔρημος]].

names.gloss: (Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Ααρων, from Hebrew ʾAhărōn, of uncertain meaning)
(Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")
(Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Φαραω Τίς ἐστιν οὗ εἰσακούσομαι τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ὥστε ἐξαποστεῖλαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ; οὐκ οἶδα τὸν κύριον καὶ τὸν Ισραηλ οὐκ ἐξαποστέλλω.
hint: Pharaoh asks whose voice he is to obey; he does not know the lord and will not release Israel.

notes.text: Who is he whose voice: the Hebrew has mî YHWH ʾăšer, who is the LORD that. The question names no one.
The sons of Israel: the Hebrew has ʾet-yiśrāʾēl, Israel.
The relative and then the pronoun again, after the Hebrew ʾăšer … bĕqōlô.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Φαραω]] who is of whom [[I will hearken|I will hearken and give ear to, I will hear, I will hearken to and give heed to|εἰσακούω]] [[of the sound|of the sound and tone, of the sound of the voice, of the cry, of the faculty of speech and discourse, of the language, of the saying|φωνή]] of him [[so as to|so as to, as to, on the condition that, and so and therefore and consequently, as and as being, since it was|ὥστε]] [[to send quite away|to send quite away, to dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]]? not [[I know|I know, I am assured, I am versed in|οἶδα]] [[the lord|the lord / master, the head, the master, the Lord, the Jehovah|κύριος]] and the [[name:Ισραηλ]] not [[I send quite away|I send quite away, I dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]].

greek: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ὁ θεὸς τῶν Εβραίων προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς· πορευσόμεθα οὖν ὁδὸν τριῶν ἡμερῶν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπως θύσωμεν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν, μήποτε συναντήσῃ ἡμῖν θάνατος ἢ φόνος.
hint: They answer that the God of the Hebrews has summoned them for a three-day journey to sacrifice, lest death befall them.

notes.text: Has called us to himself: the Hebrew has niqrāʾ ʿālênû, has met with us, which the Greek reads as from qārāʾ, to call.
To our God: the Hebrew has laYHWH ʾĕlōhênû, to the LORD our God.
Death or murder as the subject that meets them: the Hebrew has pen-yipgāʿēnû baddeber ʾô beḥāreb, lest he fall on us with pestilence or with sword.
The future, we will go, for the Hebrew cohortative nēlăkâ-nāʾ, let us go.

names.gloss: (Εβραῖος, from Hebrew ʿIbrî, usually connected with ʿēber, "the region beyond")

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου Ἵνα τί, Μωυσῆ καὶ Ααρων, διαστρέφετε τὸν λαόν μου ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων; ἀπέλθατε ἕκαστος ὑμῶν πρὸς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
hint: The king of Egypt asks Moses and Aaron why they turn the people from their work, and sends each of them back to it.

notes.text: διαστρέφω, to turn different ways, to twist, to distort: the Hebrew tapriʿû, you let loose, you release from.
Each of you to his works: the Hebrew has lĕsiblōtêkem, to your burdens.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to them [[the king|the king and chief, the hereditary king, the lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] what, [[name:Μωυσῆ]] and [[name:Ααρων]], [[you turn different ways|you turn different ways and twist about and distort, you distort and pervert|διαστρέφω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] of me [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the works|of the works, of the business, of the deeds|ἔργον]]? [[go away|go away, depart from, depart, depart from life|ἀπέρχομαι]] [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself|ἕκαστος]] of you [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the works|the works, the business, the deeds|ἔργον]] of him.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Φαραω Ἰδοὺ νῦν πολυπληθεῖ ὁ λαός· μὴ οὖν καταπαύσωμεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων.
hint: Pharaoh says the people are now numerous, and refuses to let them rest from their work.

notes.text: The people: the Hebrew has ʿam hāʾāreṣ, the people of the land.
Let us not make them rest: the Hebrew has wĕhišbattem, and you make them rest, said to Moses and Aaron.
πολυπληθέω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's multiply, citing this verse, and abound.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[now at this very time|now at this very time, now, of the present, the present time, just now and but now, as it is and as the case now stands, in this case|νῦν]] [[multiplies|multiplies, abounds|πολυπληθέω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]]; [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] [[let us lay to rest|let us lay to rest, let us put an end to, let us make to cease, let us stop and keep in check, let us put down|καταπαύω]] them [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the works|of the works, of the business, of the deeds|ἔργον]].

greek: συνέταξεν δὲ Φαραω τοῖς ἐργοδιώκταις τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν λέγων
hint: Pharaoh gives orders to the taskmasters over the people and to the scribes.

notes.text: The Hebrew adds bayyôm hahûʾ, that same day; not in this text.
γραμματεύς, a secretary or clerk, for the Hebrew šōṭĕrîm, officers. ἐργοδιώκτης, LSJ's taskmaster, one translation, plain text.

reading: [[put in order together|put in order together, drew up and put in array, arranged and organised, concocted, fixed and assessed, ordained and prescribed|συντάσσω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Φαραω]] to the taskmasters [[of the people|of the people, of the men, of the soldiers, of the land-army, of the common men, of the folk, of the Jews, of the Christians|λαός]] and [[to the secretaries|to the secretaries and clerks|γραμματεύς]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]]

greek: Οὐκέτι προστεθήσεται διδόναι ἄχυρον τῷ λαῷ εἰς τὴν πλινθουργίαν καθάπερ ἐχθὲς καὶ τρίτην ἡμέραν· αὐτοὶ πορευέσθωσαν καὶ συναγαγέτωσαν ἑαυτοῖς ἄχυρα.
hint: No more straw is to be supplied for brickmaking; the people must go and gather it for themselves.

notes.text: It will no longer be added to give, impersonal: the Hebrew lōʾ tōʾsipûn lātēt, you shall no longer give, addressed to the overseers.
As yesterday and the third day: the Hebrew kitmôl šilšōm, as before.
πλινθουργία, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's pointer to πλινθεία, brickmaking, one translation, plain text.

greek: καὶ τὴν σύνταξιν τῆς πλινθείας, ἧς αὐτοὶ ποιοῦσιν καθʼ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, ἐπιβαλεῖς αὐτοῖς, οὐκ ἀφελεῖς οὐδέν· σχολάζουσιν γάρ· διὰ τοῦτο κεκράγασιν λέγοντες Πορευθῶμεν καὶ θύσωμεν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν.
hint: The daily brick quota stays the same; Pharaoh says they are idle, and that is why they cry out to go and sacrifice.

notes.lemma: ἧς αὐτοὶ ποιοῦσιν καθʼ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν
notes.text: Which they make each day: the Hebrew has ʾăšer hēm ʿōśîm tĕmôl šilšōm, which they were making before.
The relative takes the genitive of πλινθείας before it, where ποιοῦσιν would govern the accusative.
The singular, you will lay on, you will take away: the Hebrew has the plural, tāśîmû, tigrĕʿû.
σύνταξις, an arranging, and among its senses an assigned impost: here the quota.
σχολάζω, to have leisure, for the Hebrew nirpîm, slack.

[[they have leisure|they have leisure and spare time and are at leisure, they have leisure and time to do, they loiter and linger and delay, they have rest and respite from, they cease from, they have leisure and opportunity for, they devote their time to, they devote themselves to, they devote themselves, they attend his lectures, they give lectures, they are vacant and unoccupied|σχολάζω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]]; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[have croaked|have croaked and it stands so, have screamed and shrieked and cried aloud and it stands so, have bawled aloud and it stands so, have clamoured for and it stands so|κράζω]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[let us be driven|let us be driven, let us be carried, let us go, let us walk, let us march, let us go across and pass|πορεύομαι]] and [[let us offer|let us offer, let us burn, let us sacrifice, let us slaughter and slay, let us offer sacrifices, let us celebrate with offerings|θύω]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] of us.

greek: βαρυνέσθω τὰ ἔργα τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων, καὶ μεριμνάτωσαν ταῦτα καὶ μὴ μεριμνάτωσαν ἐν λόγοις κενοῖς.
hint: Pharaoh orders the work made heavier, so that the people attend to it and not to empty words.

notes.text: One verb twice, let them care for: the Hebrew has two, wĕyaʿăśû-bāh, let them work at it, and wĕʾal-yišʿû, let them not regard.
Empty words: the Hebrew has dibrê-šāqer, words of falsehood.

greek: κατέσπευδον δὲ αὐτοὺς οἱ ἐργοδιῶκται καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγοντες Τάδε λέγει Φαραω Οὐκέτι δίδωμι ὑμῖν ἄχυρα·
hint: The taskmasters and scribes press the people, announcing Pharaoh's word that no more straw will be given.

notes.text: Were pressing them: the Hebrew has wayyēṣĕʾû, went out.
No longer do I give: the Hebrew ʾênennî nōtēn, I am not giving.

reading: [[were pressing|were pressing and urging and hastening on|κατασπεύδω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], them the taskmasters and [[the secretaries|the secretaries and clerks|γραμματεύς]] and [[were saying|were saying, were speaking, were declaring, were calling by name, were telling|λέγω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[these|these, the immediate present, here and on the spot, thus, hither and to this spot, therefore and on this account|ὅδε]] [[says|says, speaks, declares, calls by name, tells|λέγω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[no more|no more and no longer and no further|οὐκέτι]] [[I give|I give, I am ready to give and offer, I grant, I provide, I give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you [[husks|husks and chaff and bran|ἄχυρον]];

greek: αὐτοὶ ὑμεῖς πορευόμενοι συλλέγετε ἑαυτοῖς ἄχυρα ὅθεν ἐὰν εὕρητε, οὐ γὰρ ἀφαιρεῖται ἀπὸ τῆς συντάξεως ὑμῶν οὐθέν.
hint: The people must find straw wherever they can, and nothing will be taken off their quota.

notes.text: αὐτοί with ὑμεῖς: you yourselves.
From your quota: the Hebrew has mēʿăbōdatkem, from your work.
The passive, nothing is taken away, with οὐθέν its subject.

greek: καὶ διεσπάρη ὁ λαὸς ἐν ὅλῃ Αἰγύπτῳ συναγαγεῖν καλάμην εἰς ἄχυρα·
hint: The people scatter through all Egypt, gathering stubble for straw.

notes.text: In all Egypt: the Hebrew has bĕkol-ʾereṣ miṣrāyim, in all the land of Egypt.
καλάμη, the stalk, stubble, for the Hebrew qaš; ἄχυρον, husks and chaff, for teben, straw.

reading: and [[was scattered abroad|was scattered abroad, was thrown about, was squandered|διασπείρω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] [[in whole|within, inside of, and by means of whole and entire, continuous and incessant|ἐν; ὅλος]] to [[name:Αἰγύπτῳ]] [[to bring together|to bring together, to gather together, to collect, to convene, to join in one and unite, to receive into one's house, to draw together and narrow and contract, to conclude and infer|συνάγω]] [[stalk|stalk and straw of corn, stalk without the ear and stubble, remains|καλάμη]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[husks|husks and chaff and bran|ἄχυρον]].

greek: οἱ δὲ ἐργοδιῶκται κατέσπευδον αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Συντελεῖτε τὰ ἔργα τὰ καθήκοντα καθʼ ἡμέραν καθάπερ καὶ ὅτε τὸ ἄχυρον ἐδίδοτο ὑμῖν.
hint: The taskmasters keep pressing the people to finish each day's work, as when straw was supplied.

notes.text: When the straw was being given to you: the Hebrew has bihyôt hatteben, when there was straw.

notes.lemma: τὰ ἔργα τὰ καθήκοντα καθʼ ἡμέραν
notes.text: The works that are due day by day, for the Hebrew dĕbar-yôm bĕyômô, a day's matter in its day. καθήκω, to have come down to, and in the participle that which is fit, one's due.
καί as the adverb, also.

greek: καὶ ἐμαστιγώθησαν οἱ γραμματεῖς τοῦ γένους τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ οἱ κατασταθέντες ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐπιστατῶν τοῦ Φαραω λέγοντες Διὰ τί οὐ συνετελέσατε τὰς συντάξεις ὑμῶν τῆς πλινθείας, καθάπερ ἐχθὲς καὶ τρίτην ἡμέραν, καὶ τὸ τῆς σήμερον;
